name: King of Hamath
overview: The King of Hamath was a male monarch known primarily for having been defeated by the Assyrian empire. Beyond this notable defeat, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or personal background. His role is briefly mentioned without further elaboration in biblical records.
namesAndTitles: This figure is referred to simply as the 'King of Hamath,' a title indicating his rule over the city of Hamath. The name is a straightforward designation without a specific Hebrew or Greek meaning provided beyond its literal sense.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or lineage for the King of Hamath beyond what is indicated by his title and his defeat by Assyria. There are no known connections to other biblical figures documented.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Hamath's significance lies in his defeat by the Assyrian empire, which is noted in the biblical narrative. This defeat serves to highlight the power and reach of Assyria during the period and sets the stage for the unfolding events involving Assyrian dominance. His mention underscores the historical context of Assyrian expansion recorded in Scripture.
